thread:
maria: FYI ran a quick profiling pass on workspace-scoped metrics after the ACME tail spike this morning. findings + proposal below.

maria: TL;DR: tail latency correlated with kernel-selection churn + uneven KV-cache hit rates per org. proposing a workspace-scoped dashboard + RBAC toggle so SRE/product can slice without leaking org data.

jonathan: can you drop the top-level numbers? how bad was the tail? :chart_with_upwards_trend:

maria: overall p95 rose from 120ms -> 260ms for route `/v1/generate` for workspace acme-corp between 06:10-06:24 UTC. p99 hit ~1.2s due to repeated kernel fallbacks when batch size changed mid-request. KV cache hit-rate for same workspace dropped from 92% -> 57% (prefetch churn).

sasha: that matches the kernel-selection logs i looked at. heuristics try to pick quantized kernel when seq_len < 512 but some requests included a 2-step call pattern (short prompt + long context) so runtime flipped kernel + recompiled paths. cost of cache warm/evict hit tail.

maria: exact repro trace snippet (simplified):
```
[runtime] select_kernel(model=redwood-7b, seq=128) -> kernel=vq4
[batcher] append(req=R1, seq=128) -> batch=42
[request R1] during_exec: attach_prefix(context=large) -> runtime recalculates seq=1024 -> select_kernel(model=redwood-7b, seq=1024) -> kernel=fp16_cpu_fallback
[kv] probe -> miss -> fetch_from_storage -> +120ms
```

kevin: ouch. so batching heuristics + kernel-fallback + kv miss compounded. does the runtime log show kernel selection reason?

sasha: yes, there's a short enum on why we switch: `heuristic`, `spillover`, `incompatible_kv_layout`. most of these were `heuristic` with an adjacent `kv_eviction` event.

infra-bot: [alert] perf:workspace:acme-corp tail_latency.p99 > 1s (06:12 UTC) -> incident flagged (#INFR-3421) :rotating_light:

amrita: for the dashboard proposal: we should expose token-level breakdowns per-route + kernel-tag dimension + kv_cache_hit boolean. customers/SEs need read-only views for their workspace metrics, but can't access other tenants. RBAC must enforce workspace scoping at query time.

maria: proposal sketch:
- panel A: per-route token-latency waterfall (avg token queueing, token kernel exec, token kv wait) grouped by `workspace_id`
- panel B: kernel-selection waterfall (chosen_kernel, reason, fallback_count) heatmap per workspace
- panel C: KV hit-rate + ttl expirations per workspace + per-kv-partition
- control: RBAC toggle + `kernel_tag` filter for on-the-fly slicing (devs can pin to `quant-vq4` or `fp16`)

jonathan: what datasource? prometheus has token-level histograms but we may need more labels -> cardinality risk. Are we OK adding `workspace_id` label to those metrics?

amrita: we should not add high cardinality workspace_id to raw Prom histograms. instead route metrics -> labelless aggregated histos + a separate timeseries-ready OLAP table (clickhouse) with sampled token events keyed by workspace for ad-hoc slices. RBAC enforcement happens at query layer.

sasha: agreed. we can emit a sampled event stream for detailed slices: 1 in 1000 tokens (or adaptive sampling when p95/p99 thresholds breached) and push to clickhouse. then dashboards hit clickhouse for workspace-scoped views.

kevin: ok i'll own the dashboard prototype. timeline? can we do a minimal panel (kv hit rate + p95 per-route per-workspace) by EOW?

maria: EOW prototype sounds good. minimal list:
- clickhouse table schema suggestion (sampled_tokens):
```sql
CREATE TABLE sampled_tokens (
  ts DateTime,
  workspace_id String,
  route String,
  kernel_tag String,
  token_latency_ms Float32,
  kv_hit UInt8,
  seq_len UInt32
) ENGINE = MergeTree(ts, (workspace_id, route), 8192)
```
- grafana panel that queries p95(token_latency_ms) grouped by route for a given workspace_id (variable)
```sql
SELECT quantileExact(0.95)(token_latency_ms) AS p95
FROM sampled_tokens
WHERE workspace_id = '{{workspace_id}}' AND ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
GROUP BY route
```

amrita: RBAC note: the query layer must drop any wildcard workspace variables unless caller has `view:all_workspaces`. implement at proxy level with token-scoped claims. also add tenant_id hash column for fast lookup and no joins.

jonathan: two quick asks: 1) can we add a kernel fallback counter as a derived metric (per-request)? 2) add sequence-length histogram per workspace to spot when requests jump mid-flight.

sasha: 1) yes runtime already emits `kernel_fallback_count` per-request, we can sample it into clickhouse. 2) seq histogram we can approximate via sampled events + a lightweight per-workspace histogram aggregate (not labeled per-token) in Prom for quick alerts.

kevin: i'll sketch panels tonight. will also add a guarded example link for customer-facing view with obfuscated workspace name.

maria: action items:
- kevin to deliver clickhouse panel prototype + example workspace read-only view -> due Fri EOD (KEVIN)
- sasha to add adaptive sampling + ensure kernel_fallback_count export -> 2d (SASHA)
- amrita to draft RBAC enforcement at query proxy + claim mapping -> 3d (AMRITA)
- jonathan to add alert rule for kernel-selection churn + kv-hit dips -> 1d (JONATHAN)
- maria to attach incident trace to #INFR-3421 and follow up with ACME SEs -> today (MARIA)

amrita: quick question: do we want customers to be able to toggle kernel_tag in customer UI or only internal? my vote: internal-only for now, customers can request via support.

kеvin: +1 internal-only for the first rollout. too many knobs for customers. :thumbsup:

maria: agreed. keeping kernel_tag filters internal for now. we'll expose read-only KPIs to customers (p50/p95/p99 routes + kv hit) with obfuscated kernel info.

jonathan: any perf-regression risk from sampling? need to confirm sampling path is async and non-blocking.

sasha: sampling uses existing async telemetry pipeline, negligible overhead at 1/1k. adaptive sampling will bump to 1/100 when p99 > threshold but still async.

maria: thanks everyone. filing the dashboard ticket + linking infra alert: #INFR-3421. i'll post updates in this thread. :white_check_mark:
